clue.text: High-flier in Tory party close to donor

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative, abbreviated CON
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so take the end of donor

parts.note: its last letter is R

explanation.surface: A rising Conservative star at a party fundraiser cosies up to a wealthy backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests an ambitious politician, but it is the bird. Condor is also a London bicycle maker, one of the puzzle's hidden bike brands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean condor is a huge vulture that soars at great altitude, so it is literally a bird that flies high.

clue.text: Annually repeated circuit round the centre of Paris was gripping

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, here from Paris

parts.note: its middle letter is R
bit is the past tense of bite, to grip with the teeth

explanation.surface: Something circling central Paris once a year held people in its grip, like a race or parade.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth's path round the Sun is a closed circuit completed once every year.

clue.text: Rogue Mary dated had fantasies before bedtime

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wild or out of control, so the letters that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman whose date was a rascal lay awake fantasising before she went to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before bedtime' is a link that fits the surface: daydreams happen while awake. The past tense is spelt with -T, as in learnt.
explanation.definitionFit: To daydream is to indulge in pleasant fantasies while awake, so the past tense means had fantasies.

clue.text: Yorkshire river leaks out of its banks

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its two edges, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: dribbles means leaks or trickles out

explanation.surface: A northern river bursts its banks and floods.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the outer D and S from DRIBBLES. The Ribble rises in North Yorkshire and flows through Lancashire; Ribble is also a bicycle brand from the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a real watercourse rising in the Yorkshire Dales before flowing west to the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Nothing to do with millions in retirement for old King's Counsel

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
re means concerning, about
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A retired King's Counsel, a senior barrister, claims to have nothing to do with his millions.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Counsel suggests a senior lawyer, but the king here is Arthur and his counsellor is the wizard. Merlin is also a bike maker in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend the wizard was the trusted adviser of King Arthur, so he counselled an old king.

clue.text: Lame cooking with ordinary recipe, ultimately humdrum grub

indicators.note: cooking means being prepared or worked on, so the letters of lame are rearranged

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: its last letter is M

explanation.surface: Poor cooking from an ordinary recipe produces boring food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like slang for food, which fits the cooking story, but it is the insect larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A mealworm is the larva of a darkling beetle, and a grub is any such soft insect larva.

clue.text: E.g. Mamil when sporting lurid ergonomic clothes

indicators.note: sporting means wearing or displaying, so the answer is carried within the words that follow
the phrase clothes, covers, the letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A middle-aged man in garish, body-shaped Lycra out on his bike.
explanation.walkthrough: MAMIL stands for Middle-Aged Man In Lycra, a British jokey term for keen road cyclists.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mamil is a type of cyclist, so he is an example of someone who sits on and steers a bike.

clue.text: Filbert's getting on trousers at home, occupied with thoughts

parts.note: the setter is Filbert, so Filbert's is I'm, i.e. I am

indicators.note: used as a verb, trousers means pockets or takes in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: getting on means growing old, ageing
in means at home

explanation.surface: The setter, pulling on trousers at home, is lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets. AGING is spelt without the E here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forming pictures in the mind is busy with ideas, so their head is occupied with thoughts.

clue.text: Chatty homosexual bishops are boring

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the bishops bore into the other word

parts.note: gay means homosexual
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two of them are BB

explanation.surface: A talkative gay man finds the bishops tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull but means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gabby talks a great deal, so the word is an informal synonym for talkative.

clue.text: Two soldiers, one very small, one very tall

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
an ant is a tiny insect, and soldier ants exist, hence the clue's two soldiers

explanation.surface: A pair of soldiers, one tiny and one towering.
explanation.walkthrough: The two soldiers are a GI and a soldier ant. Giant is also a bicycle brand in the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant is a person or creature of enormous height, the opposite of the tiny insect.

clue.text: Rocky and Rambo director, perhaps

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, so the letters of the next words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Who directed the Stallone films Rocky and Rambo?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like the film title but is the anagram signal. A company director sits on the board, so he is, perhaps, a board man; Chris Boardman also lends his name to a bike brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A company director is a member of the board, so playfully he is a man of the board; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Fictional character Mighty Mouse keeps heading skyward

indicators.note: in a down clue heading skyward means reading upwards, i.e. backwards
the phrase keeps, holds, a run of its own letters

explanation.surface: The cartoon superhero Mighty Mouse keeps flying up into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth can be a fictitious person or thing, someone who exists only in story or imagination.

clue.text: Radiation left wolf with great metamorphoses

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a transformation, so the letters change shape into a new word

explanation.surface: A great werewolf transforms and leaves behind a glow.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterglow is the light that remains in the sky after sunset, radiation left behind once the source has gone.

clue.text: Painter occupying gallery finally calling for oils?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
in means occupying, as in in residence

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of gallery

parts.note: its last letter is Y

explanation.surface: An artist working in a gallery asks for oil paints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oils' looks like oil paint, but here it is oilskins, the waterproofs worn in wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather is when you need oilskins, so a day of showers calls for waterproof clothing.

clue.text: A red, one drunk by abstemious Scot

indicators.note: drunk by means swallowed by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: TT means teetotal, never drinking alcohol
I is the Roman numeral for one
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A teetotal Scotsman is offered a glass of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A red' suggests a glass of wine, but it is a hair colour named after the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is a bright reddish-auburn shade, named from the Venetian painter's use of it.

clue.text: Italian mounting show with extravagant sculpture etc.

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing, so the pieces read upwards

parts.note: to air is to show or display
OTT is over the top, extravagant
sculpture and similar works are art

explanation.surface: An Italian is staging a show featuring lavish sculpture and other art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' looks like a person but is short for an Italian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian eatery; we say we are going for an Italian, meaning a meal at one.

clue.text: Atlantic expedition leader's spoken, rowers stripped

indicators.note: stripped means losing the outer covering, so the first and last letters of the combined pieces go

parts.note: oral means spoken
an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A transatlantic explorer gives a talk while his oarsmen strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Raleigh led expeditions across the Atlantic to the Americas. Raleigh is also a famous British bicycle maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan adventurer sponsored and led voyages to Virginia and Guiana across the ocean.

clue.text: Line meandering in sandal a clue to what left it?

indicators.note: meandering means wandering in curves, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A wiggly line on a sandal is a clue to the creature that crawled over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures the silvery slime trail on a sandal left outdoors; that trail is the clue to its maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail that lives on the ground leaves a trail of slime behind it, so it is the creature that left the line.

clue.text: Sponge saddle cover?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cadge or sponge off others
second meaning: a backside sits on and covers the saddle

explanation.walkthrough: 'saddle cover' looks like a bicycle accessory, but the rider's backside is what covers a saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it is slang for scrounge, and as a noun British slang for the buttocks that sit on a saddle.

clue.text: South Kensington location's empty but hosting special prom just after

indicators.note: hosting means having a guest inside, so one piece goes into the other
empty means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters of but

parts.note: emptied it gives BT

indicators.note: special here means altered or unusual, so the letters of prom are rearranged

parts.note: on can mean just after, as in on arrival

explanation.surface: A spot in South Kensington is deserted except when it hosts the Proms just afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are summer concerts at the Royal Albert Hall in South Kensington, London; Brompton is the neighbouring district and also a folding-bike maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Brompton is the London district around South Kensington, home to the Brompton Oratory.

clue.text: Become more suitable for steady cycling?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to become someone is to suit them and show them off well
second meaning: more level, with fewer hills, so easier to ride at an even pace

explanation.walkthrough: 'Become' looks like 'turn into', but it is the old verb meaning to suit, as in 'that hat becomes you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to show someone off well, and the comparative adjective describes a road with fewer hills.

clue.text: Experienced fellow allowed to have learner demoted

indicators.note: in a down clue demoted means moved lower, so the learner's letter drops to the bottom of its word

parts.note: let means allowed
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A man was permitted to have his trainee lowered in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Felt is also a bicycle brand in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is the past tense of feel, and to have felt something is to have experienced it.

clue.text: Inscrutable character of endlessly kind mother

indicators.note: endlessly means both ends are cut off

parts.note: benign means kind and gentle
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An inscrutable personality belonging to a kind mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both ends of BENIGN to get ENIG.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mysterious, puzzling person whose thoughts cannot be read.

clue.text: Gas shipment not carbon neutral

indicators.note: not means without, so the carbon is taken out

parts.note: cargo is a ship's load, a shipment
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
N is the abbreviation for neutral, as on a gear lever

explanation.surface: A shipment of gas that is not carbon neutral, an environmental gripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbon neutral' reads as an eco phrase, but carbon and neutral are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert noble gas that makes up about one per cent of air.

clue.text: Either aspect of flagellation that hurts temporarily

parts.note: an aspect is a side, and the two sides of the word flagellation are its first and last letters, so either one of them is spelt out as this letter, or, that letter
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: Either side of a whipping hurts, but only for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Either aspect of flagellation' literally: the word's two sides are F and N, so either of them is 'F or N', giving FORN. Then add OW.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something for the time being, until things change, means doing it temporarily.

clue.text: Last bit of fruit tortured soul eats?

definitions.text: Last bit of fruit tortured soul eats?

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so the letter goes within the other word
tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters of soul are rearranged
the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its last letter is T

explanation.surface: A tormented soul nibbles the last piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey the lotus-eaters ate a fruit that made them forget their troubles, just what a tortured soul would want.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus of Greek myth is the fruit eaten to bring blissful forgetfulness of sorrow.

clue.text: Wet horse, therefore yard providing blanket

indicators.note: providing a blanket means wrapping round, so the outer pieces enclose the horse

parts.note: so means therefore
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A rain-soaked horse in the yard needs a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soggy is soaked through with water, so it is very damp.

clue.text: Low winds when cycling, good change from high?

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

indicators.note: cycling means letters going round from one end to the other, here two letters from the end of winds go to the front

explanation.surface: Feeling low, a cyclist battling the wind longs for a good change from a high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' and 'high' look like moods, but low is the cow's call; the question mark marks the definition as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden shift from elation to gloom is a swing in emotional state, so a change from high is an example.

clue.text: Extremely snappy single speed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single
rate means speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: A single-speed bike is described as extremely zippy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snappy' suggests quick, matching single speed, but here it means short-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who snaps at people is angry, so very snappy describes a furious person.

clue.text: Put hand in bog for bully

indicators.note: put signals placing one piece somewhere, here into the bog
in shows the hand goes inside the wet ground

parts.note: a fen is low marshy ground, a bog
right is a hand, as in on your right

explanation.surface: Pushing someone's hand into a bog is what a bully does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bully' looks like a noun but is the verb, to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully is to cow or intimidate someone, which means scaring them.

clue.text: More profit, America first

indicators.note: first means the America piece comes before the profit

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: An America-first slogan demanding even more profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More profit' reads as one phrase, but 'More' alone is the definition, in the sense of once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something again means doing it once more, an additional time.

clue.text: Bog over there, river down here?

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet, and can is American slang for the same
yon is an old word meaning over there

explanation.surface: Someone points out a toilet over there, and a river down below.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a descriptive definition: a canyon is where the river lies far below you.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge cut by a river that runs along its floor, far below the rim.

clue.text: More foxy women tell stories in Irish

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: to lie is to tell stories, tall tales

explanation.surface: Craftier women spin yarns in Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foxy' suggests attractive, but here it means cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox is proverbially cunning, so foxier means craftier, more cunning.
